title: Engineer Sequencer: Quickplay Notelets (Draft)
body:
Goal: give sellers + SEs a tiny, engineer-friendly slide pack that sequences the minimal tech and econ talking points for a 15–30 minute pilot conversation.

Notes on tone and use: short bullets + speaker cues (callouts for when to drop a demo or escalate to CE). This is intentionally compact — think pocket slide deck you can skim before a call.

Slide 1 — One-line opener (30s):
- Title: "Why Redwood Inference for predictable LLM economics"
- Speaker cue: "I want to show you how we get consistent latency and predictable cost across hosted vs dedicated deployments in short order."
- Quick stat to lead with: "average token latency reduction 23% in live benchmarks vs baseline (customer pilot)" — only use if you have an up-to-date bench link.

Slide 2 — Sequencer: 3 conversation phases (visual timeline)
- Phase A: Qualify latency & scale (3–6 mins) — ask: peak concurrency? percentiles that matter (p50/p95/p99)? max sequence length?
- Phase B: Pilot constraints & acceptance criteria (5–10 mins) — define SLAs, throughput, cost target per 1k requests
- Phase C: Migration & fallback plan (3–5 mins) — canary windows, fallback models, QoS trade-offs

Speaker note: move fast through A if they already gave metrics in discovery. Use A to bind them to measurable goals.

Slide 3 — Quick qualifying checklist (use as a checklist on call)
- Real work item: "Do you have p95 latency target in ms?"
- Data isolation: "Are requests regulated / require VPC or KMS?"
- Payload patterns: "Many short chats vs few long prompts?"
- Cost sensitivity: "Willing to trade 10% quality for 30% cost reduction?"

Slide 4 — Pilot topology options (sketch + 1-line tradeoffs)
- Hosted API (fastest onboarding): good for low regulatory risk, small pilots, pay-as-you-go
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pool): good for predictable throughput and consistent perf
- Private (VPC / on-prem): for regulated data, compliance, or offline/air-gapped needs

Speaker cue: if the customer mentions SOC2/PCI/PHI, pivot to Private topologies immediately and loop in CS/Legal.

Slide 5 — Built-in fallbacks sellers need to mention (scripted lines)
- "If latency spikes we can automatically route to a lower-cost but faster quantized variant while preserving output semantics."
- "We can set model rollouts to canary (5–20%) and auto-fallback if quality drops on our eval suite."
- Demo cue: show routing policy UI and a canary status timeline (30s demo).

Slide 6 — Micro-econ knobs (3 bullets, use numbers)
- Batching: "Depending on your QPS we can shave 20–50% off GPU token cost by continuous batching; tradeoff is added queuing latency"
- KV/prefix caching: "For chat-heavy flows caching previous KV states can cut token use by ~30% for repeated contexts"
- Quantization profile: "We recommend INT8 for most inference; we can A/B with INT4 for cost experiments"

Call script: "If cost is the blocker, can we set a 2-week INT8 experiment on non-critical traffic and measure user metrics?"

Slide 7 — Fast triage map (if pilot starts failing)
- Symptom: rising latency p95 -> first check: batching config and autoscale headroom
- Symptom: quality regression after model swap -> run recent prompt set evals (linked) and rollback to previous variant
- Symptom: tail errors / 5xxs -> check routing (region), capacity pool logs, and fallback policy status

Quick hits: include command/console shortcuts for SEs:
- "redwood metrics query --range 15m --agg p95"
- Link to runbook: confluence:pilot-runbook-quick-triage (use when escalating)

Slide 8 — Minimal pilot plan (14 days) — canonical example to propose on call
- Day 0–1: onboarding + sample traffic capture (agent to send curl + sample JSON)
- Day 2–4: baseline run on hosted: measure p50/p95, token cost per 1k, throughput under 50% target QPS
- Day 5–9: enable dedicated burst / latency tuning, apply batching and caching profiles
- Day 10–12: optional quantization experiment on non-critical route (A/B)
- Day 13–14: evaluate, produce recommendations + next-step contract (if Dedicated desired)

Speaker script: "This is light — our goal is a clear decision point at day 14: keep hosted and optimize, or commit to Dedicated with targets locked."

Slide 9 — Top 10 objection snippets (for sellers to read fast)
- Objection: "I need absolute latency guarantees." -> "We offer Dedicated pools with SLA targets and multi-region fallback; we can model your peak trace and simulate."
- Objection: "We can't send data out." -> "Private VPC / on-prem available with KMS integration; we'll coordinate with your security lead."
- Objection: "Cost unpredictable." -> "We provide per-token breakdowns, cost simulators, and reserved capacity options to fix unit economics."

Slide 10 — Example micro-demo script (60–90s)
- Show Console -> Model catalog -> Open model variant -> open routing policies -> simulate a traffic spike and show auto-fallback to quantized variant
- Key phrasing: "Notice the cost meter and the service fallback — we can run this scenario against your trace and share the output."

Appendix (talking points and links):
- Quick GH PR to reference: github.com/redwood-inference/engineer-playbooks/pilot-scripts (if public/internal link available)
- Sample eval prompt set: confluence:evalsets/pilot-chat-100
- Slack thread to post to when you need an on-call SRE: #sre-oncall (include the pilot id)

Open items / TODO (internal):
- Add up-to-date benchmark number (ask research for p95/throughput canonical table) — assigned Priya
- Create one-click sample trace uploader in Console (product wishlist) — log JIRA GTMSUP-4123
- Record 90s demo video, host link in the slide footer

Free-form notes to self (choppy):
- want a single-pane "sequencer" view in Console — shows three-phase timeline + quick toggles to run experiments
- sellers like 2-line rebuttals and a 60s demo script. keep both on the first screen
- keep conservatively worded econ numbers until we validate with Research

Example quick email follow-up (paste into Gmail after pilot call):
Subject: Next steps + Day 0 checklist (Redwood pilot)
Hi <Name>,
Thanks for the time today — re cc'ing our SE for onboarding. Attached below is the 14-day plan we discussed and the two sample curl commands to capture a trace. Can you confirm the p95 target and whether the workload is chat-heavy or single-shot prompts?
Thanks,
Jordan

----
Version history: draft v0.1 — lightweight, intended for rapid field feedback. Please add notes inline if you tried the 14-day plan and what we should adjust (esp. timing for bigger enterprise IT approvals).
